thread:
Anya (Marketing): Quick sync 1 — need a tight benchmark narrative for the launch. Goal: one short social post, a 3-slide webinar storyboard, and a single micro-chart for the docs. Core message: small latency wins -> outsized cost savings at scale. Who wants to own framing + chart asks?

Ravi (Growth): I got the social copy. Proposed headline: "Faster tokens, lower bills: how latency tuning shrinks inference costs". Need concrete numbers to land it.

Jon (Product): Slide plan:
- Slide 1: p95 latency vs $/1M tokens (line chart) showing how tail latency drives cost via smaller effective batching and more fallback work.
- Slide 2: Cached vs uncached comparison (side-by-side bars) with $/100k requests.
- Slide 3: Routing playbook table: cost impact vs SLA (hosted, dedicated, private).

Leah (Design): Chart specs: small footprint (900x540), two-color palette (brand blue + charcoal). Axis labels: "p95 latency (ms)" and "$/1M tokens". Add dashed SLO at 200ms. I'll mock both wide deck and square blog embed.

Sam (Data): I'll run experiments and produce real points. Plan: 3 models (7B/13B/70B), synthetic workload seeded with median customer token distribution. Measure p50/p95/p99 and compute cost per 100k tokens with/without KV prefix caching. ETA: CSV by Thu EOD.

Anya (Marketing): For social post we need 1-liner + subline + CTA. Ravi, can you draft? Tone: product-forward and shareable.

Ravi (Growth): Draft: "Cut inference bills by up to 3x 1 optimize latency, not just model size. See our benchmark + webinar." Subline: "Live demo + micro-charts: how caching, batching, and routing change LLM economics. Register: https://redwood.example/webinar"

Jon (Product): Add footnotes on assumptions (token length distro, concurrency, embeddings included?). Also show a tiny policy flow that keeps user latency low while routing noninteractive jobs to cheaper variants.

Leah (Design): Filenames: latency_micro_v1.png (deck), latency_micro_embed_v1.png (blog). Need the CSV to annotate points and call out the single-big-number caption: e.g., "Latency tuning + caching cut $/1M tokens by 45% in our median workload". That caption should be the main shareable stat.

Sam (Data): CSV schema I'll produce: model, run_id, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, tokens_per_request, cost_per_1M_tokens_usd, cached_boolean, batch_factor, kv_hit_rate. Sample row:
```
13B, run-2026-03-26-01, 48, 210, 480, 92, 12.34, true, 4, 0.78
```
I'll compute mean savings and 95% CI and include a small table in the deliverable.

Anya (Marketing): Inbound routing: two lead buckets:
- Econ Curious: downloads one-pager -> automated nurture flow.
- Sales Warm: requests dedicated benchmarks or private deploy -> tag to AE queue with "benchmark-request".
CTA on landing should mirror social language.

Ravi (Growth): Add utm_source=bench_launch on links. Include a hidden field to flag high-QPS interest (qps > 50) so SDRs can prioritize. Also include one form question: "Are you evaluating performance at scale? (Yes/No)".

Jon (Product): Add a tiny reproducible snippet on docs page so engineers can sanity-check the benchmark:
```
# run synthetic workload
python run_bench.py --model redwood-13b --concurrency 8 --tokens 1024 --cache true
```
Keep it minimal.

Leah (Design): UX nit: caption under chart with the single-most-actionable stat. Keep the big percent as the hero.

Sam (Data): Also include quantization comparator (quantized vs non-quantized). I'll add two rows per run for quantized true/false. Timeline unchanged.

Anya (Marketing): Owners & deadlines:
- Benchmark CSV + numbers: Sam 1 Thu EOD (1762670000)
- Slide + micro-chart mock: Leah 1 Fri AM
- Social + landing copy + form: Ravi 1 Fri EOD
- Product notes + code snippet: Jon 1 Fri EOD
- Final review & publish checklist: Anya 1 next Tue AM

Ravi (Growth): I'll also make a 30s teaser video for LinkedIn/X (screen capture of the three slides). Need mock by Fri noon to hit next-week cadence. :rocket:

Jon (Product): Quick ask: include a mini-variant comparing quantized vs non-quantized runs as a callout?

Sam (Data): Yes, will include quantization flag and compute deltas.

Anya (Marketing): Sounds good. If no objections we'll proceed with this plan. I'll post a short publish checklist once artifacts arrive. :thumbsup:
